subject: Renewal: augment reserved GPUs & add EU/APAC pools — term amendment & failover playbook
messages:
From: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@parkside.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion: reserved capacity and global pools

Hi Jordan —

Our renewal for Reserved Capacity is coming up in March and the product team wants to expand our footprint as part of the next term. Current ask: add dedicated capacity in EU and APAC (we want regional pools to serve local latency-sensitive users) and increase total reserved GPUs to support a 2x peak growth plan.

Key asks up-front:
- Target additional capacity: +24 GPUs (16 EU, 8 APAC) as reserved pools.
- Throughput expectations: baseline 400–600 tokens/sec aggregate for peak windows; need 95th pct latency targets by region.
- Failover behavior: when a regional pool is saturated, we need automatic routing/fallback and clear billing semantics.
- Term: open to 12 or 24 months if price & SLAs align.

Can we kick off a renewal/expansion plan and get a draft amendment + rough pricing? Procurement (cc'd) will need an SOW/DocuSign-ready amendment and PO timeline.

Thanks,
Emma Jensen
VP Product
Parkside Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@parkside.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: reserved capacity and global pools

Emma — thanks for the clear asks. High-level proposal below; attaching a draft amendment and a one-page cost summary for your review. (Attachment: redwood-amendment-draft-v2.pdf)

Proposal summary:
- Capacity: add 16 x reserved GPUs in eu-west (regional pool) + 8 x reserved GPUs in apac-southeast (regional pool).
- Throughput / Sizing: we size the pools to sustain 500 tokens/sec aggregate for the added capacity at 95th percentile on typical 512-token requests. We can update once you provide production token distribution.
- Latency SLOs (95th): EU target <220ms; APAC target <260ms.
- Failover: automatic cross-region fallback policy to nearest compatible model variant (warm-standby routing to us-west) with a configurable fallback cap to limit cross-region traffic.
- Billing: incremental reserved capacity billed pro-rata from effective date of amendment; burst capacity still available at on-demand rates if needed.
- Term options: 12-mo (standard price) or 24-mo (8% term discount + 6% multi-pool commit discount).
- Runbook / Canary: recommend a 4-week canary with 10–30% traffic shift to new pools, plus a 2-week performance stabilization window.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm counts (16 EU / 8 APAC) and term preference (12 vs 24).
2) Vivek will follow with a concise failover/runbook note and any networking prerequisites.
3) I'll send an amendment + DocuSign link once we align on scope and billing terms.

Cc’ing procurement & operations to keep them in the loop.

—Jordan
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@parkside.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Susan Li <susan.li@parkside.ai>, procurement@parkside.ai
Date: Thu, 07 Jan 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: reserved capacity and global pools

Thanks Jordan. A few clarifying questions from product & procurement:

1) Failover semantics — when EU pool is saturated and traffic routes to US, do we pay on the reserved commitment only, or are we charged additional on-demand egress/usage for failover traffic?
2) Networking — what peering or egress constraints should we expect for cross-region fallback? Will there be any extra egress cost on our Azure/GCP side?
3) Compliance — we need to confirm the Private deployment/KMS options for EU data residency; SOC 2 evidence is required as part of the renewal packet.

Procurement (Susan) will take the lead on the contractual side once we have the amendment.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Emma

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@parkside.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: reserved capacity and global pools — technical notes

Emma — quick technical notes to address your questions: (attaching runbook-eu-apac-failover.xlsx)

- Billing during failover: reserved commitments cover the allocated capacity in region. If traffic overflows into a different region beyond the configured fallback cap, that overflow is billed at on-demand token rates. We can set a hard cap to avoid surprise billing; anything beyond that will require explicit approval.

- Routing / networking: fallback is performed at the Redwood edge routing layer. For Private deployments we require peering and explicit egress configuration; for Hosted API fallback we traverse our inter-region backbone — no additional egress invoicing on Redwood’s side, but you should validate cloud provider egress if you host nearby proxies.

- Data residency / compliance: EU-resident inference is supported via customer-specific EU pool (data plane stays in eu-west). KMS integration for key management is available for Private deployments; SOC 2 package (latest) is attached in the Drive link I shared previously.

- Operational runbook (summary):
  * Canary: 4 weeks, start at 10% traffic shift ramp to 30% over 10 days.
  * Monitoring: 95th latency, token/sec, error budget (1% target).
  * Failover play: automated reroute + alert to ops + traffic throttle if cross-region usage > 20% of added pool capacity.

If that looks good I’ll produce a short appendix to the amendment describing the fallback cap and throttling behavior. Happy to jump on a brief technical call.

—Vivek
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
